user.title: Tibber Energy Tariff
user.description: Connect the Smart Battery Optimizer to your Tibber account. Find your API token at app.tibber.com → Account → Developer.

data_description.tibber_api_token: Your personal API token from app.tibber.com → Account → Developer. Enables fetching hourly price forecasts.
data_description.tibber_price_sensor: Sensor from the Tibber integration showing the current electricity price (e.g. sensor.tibber_pulse_current_hour_price).
data_description.tibber_consumption_sensor: Sensor measuring current power drawn from the grid in watts (positive = import from grid).
data_description.tibber_export_sensor: Sensor measuring current power fed into the grid in watts. May be the same sensor as consumption with negative values – enter it separately regardless.

battery.title: Battery
battery.description: Configure your home battery. These values control how aggressively the battery is charged and discharged.

data.battery_max_limit_pct: Maximum State of Charge for Grid Charging (%)

data_description.battery_level_sensor: Sensor reporting current battery charge level in percent (0–100).
data_description.battery_capacity_wh: Total capacity of your battery in watt-hours. Example: a 5 kWh battery = 5000 Wh.
data_description.battery_min_limit_pct: The battery will not discharge below this level – kept as emergency reserve. Recommended: 10–20 %.
data_description.battery_max_limit_pct: The battery will be charged from the grid up to this level (at cheap prices). Solar surplus can charge beyond this. Recommended: 80–95 %.
data_description.battery_efficiency_pct: Round-trip efficiency of the battery charge/discharge cycle. Typical: 90 % (100 Wh in → 90 Wh usable).
data_description.solar_charge_state_sensor: Optional: Sensor from your battery charger reporting charge stage (e.g. 'Absorption', 'Float', 'Bulk'). Improves forecast accuracy.

solar_inverter.title: Solar & Inverter
solar_inverter.description: Connect the optimizer to your solar array. Then choose what type of storage or inverter you have.

data_description.solar_power_sensor: All sensors measuring current solar production in watts. Select multiple if you have multiple strings or inverters.
data_description.balcony_power_sensor: Optional: Sensor for a plug-in balcony power plant (micro-PV without battery connection) measured separately.
data_description.max_inverter_power_w: Maximum allowed output of the inverter in watts. In Germany legally limited to 800 W for plug-in PV systems.
data_description.inverter_profile: Choose your device type: OpenDTU/Hoymiles, an all-in-one powerstation (EcoFlow, Anker, Bluetti...) or a generic switch.

inverter_opendtu.title: OpenDTU / Hoymiles Configuration
inverter_opendtu.description: Connect the optimizer to your OpenDTU inverter.

data_description.opendtu_turn_on_button: Button entity in Home Assistant that turns the inverter on (starts battery discharge).
data_description.opendtu_turn_off_button: Button entity in Home Assistant that turns the inverter off (stops battery discharge).
data_description.opendtu_producing_sensor: Binary sensor indicating whether the inverter is currently producing power (true = on, false = off).
data_description.opendtu_output_sensor: Sensor reporting the current output power of the inverter in watts.
data_description.opendtu_dpl_mode_select: Optional: Entity to control the 'Dynamic Power Limiter' mode in OpenDTU. If set, the inverter is throttled smoothly instead of hard on/off switching.

inverter_powerstation.title: Powerstation (EcoFlow / Anker / Bluetti ...)
inverter_powerstation.description: Configure your all-in-one powerstation. The optimizer controls the discharge power directly via a number entity.

data_description.ps_discharge_power_entity: Number entity on your powerstation controlling maximum discharge power in watts. The optimizer sets this to 0 W (off) or to the configured maximum (on).
data_description.ps_charge_power_entity: Optional: Number entity for maximum charge power. If set, the optimizer increases charge power when the battery should not discharge.
data_description.ps_ac_output_switch: Optional: Switch that enables/disables the AC output of the powerstation (e.g. 'Enable AC output' on EcoFlow devices).
data_description.ps_output_sensor: Optional: Sensor measuring current output power in watts. Improves excess power calculations.

inverter_generic.title: Generic Switch
inverter_generic.description: Control your inverter or storage via a simple on/off switch in Home Assistant.

data_description.generic_inverter_switch: Switch entity that turns your inverter or storage on and off. Any switch available in HA can be used here.
data_description.generic_output_sensor: Optional: Sensor measuring current output power in watts. Improves excess power calculations.

system.title: System Parameters
system.description: Core parameters of your energy system used for forecasting and optimization calculations.

data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity from a Home Assistant weather integration (e.g. weather.home). Cloud cover forecast is used for the solar yield prediction.
data_description.base_load_w: Average household power consumption excluding large appliances, in watts. Tip: Read from Tibber app as average overnight consumption.
data_description.solar_peak_w: Nominal peak power of all installed solar panels in watts (sum of all panel ratings). Example: 10 × 400 W panels = 4000 W.
data_description.extreme_price_threshold: Price threshold (€/kWh) above which electricity is considered 'extremely expensive'. The optimizer prefers battery discharge above this level. Typical: 0.35–0.50 €/kWh.
data_description.excluded_power_sensors: Optional: Power sensors of large consumers to exclude when calculating normal household consumption. Example: EV charger, heat pump.

excess.title: Excess Power Consumers
excess.description: Devices that are switched on automatically when more solar power is being produced than consumed. All fields are optional – only configure what you have.

data.early_excess_min_battery_pct: Minimum Battery Level for Early Consumers (%)

data_description.primary_excess_consumers: Switches for devices that are turned on first when solar surplus is available (e.g. washing machine, dishwasher). Highest priority.
data_description.secondary_excess_consumers: Switches for devices that are turned on only when surplus remains after primary consumers. Second priority.
data_description.early_excess_consumers: Switches for devices that may be switched on early in the morning when the battery is sufficiently charged – even before full solar surplus is available.
data_description.early_excess_expected_power_w: Typical power consumption of early morning consumers in watts. Used to assess whether enough solar power is expected.
data_description.early_excess_min_battery_pct: Minimum battery charge level before early consumers may be switched on. Protects against discharging with insufficient solar yield.
data_description.excess_min_run_time_minutes: Minimum runtime in minutes before an excess consumer is switched off again. Prevents rapid on/off cycling and protects appliances.
data_description.excess_external_inverter: Optional: Switches connected to an external inverter (not OpenDTU). These are not subject to OpenDTU power limits.
data_description.smart_devices: Optional: JSON configuration for devices with schedules and learning functions (advanced feature for experienced users).

grid_charger.title: Grid Charger
grid_charger.description: Configure charging the battery from the grid. The optimizer charges automatically when the Tibber price is especially cheap. Leave both fields empty if you do not have a grid charger.

data_description.grid_charger_switch: Optional: Switch entity that turns the grid charger for your battery on and off. Leave empty if you do not want to charge from the grid.
data_description.grid_charger_power_w: Charging power of the grid charger in watts. Used to plan grid charging at cheap Tibber prices.
